On Italian doors: SPINGERE = PUSH. Picture yourself SPINning a door open by pushing it.
Think 'gyrate' and 'gyroscope': things that TURN. Gira a destra = Turn right.
Think 'firm': you stand FIRM and stop. La fermata = the bus stop.
Just like 'prepare'. Preparo la cena = I'm making dinner.
Think 'polish': you clean until it shines.
Think 'vigil': staying AWAKE. Mi sveglio = I wake up. Gli sounds like 'lli' in million.
Think 'altitude': getting higher. Alzati! = Get up!
Think 'sedentary' and 'sediment' (what settles and sits). Siediti! = Sit down!
Think 'mandate': an order you SEND out. Ti mando = I'll send you.
Just like 'receive'. Ho ricevuto = I received.
Just like 'offer'. Offro io! = My treat!
Think 'rupture' and 'interrupt' (to break in). Ho rotto = I broke.
Sounds like 'tally-ah': you CUT notches to keep a tally. Tagliatelle = cut pasta ribbons!
Think 'nascent' and 'native': just born. Sono nato = I was born.
I was born in Santo André.
Think 'spouse'. Ci sposiamo! = We're getting married!
Sounds like 'batch': a whole BATCH of kisses. Un bacio = a kiss (and Baci chocolates!).
Sounds like 'sonny, yeah': sonny lies in bed DREAMING. Gn = 'ny' in canyon.
Just like 'serve'. A cosa serve? = What's it for?
Think 'count' and 'account'. Conta fino a dieci = Count to ten.
Just like 'repeat'. Può ripetere? = Could you repeat that?
Sounds like 'shell-yeah': you CHOOSE the best shell. Sce = 'sheh', gli = 'lly'.
Think 'incendiary': setting things alight. Accendi la luce = Turn on the light.
to turn off / to put out
Sounds like 'spend near': you SPEND the night near a fire, then PUT it OUT.
Think 'encounter'. Ti incontro al bar = I'll meet you at the café.
I'll meet you at the café.
Just like 'visit'. Visitiamo Roma = We're visiting Rome.
Think 'inhabit' and 'habitat'. Dove abiti? = Where do you live?
Sounds like 'spoil ya': a MISTAKE spoils everything. Ho sbagliato = I got it wrong.
'Basta!' = Enough! The word Italian parents shout. Basta così = That's enough.
Think 'value' and 'valid'. Ne vale la pena = It's worth it.
Backwards from English: Mi manchi = you are missing to me = I miss you. Think 'man can't' find something.
Just like 'occupy'. Occupato = taken / busy (on toilet doors too).
Think 'salvage' and 'salvation'. Mi hai salvato! = You saved me!
The '-cide' in 'homicide' and 'suicide' means kill. Uccidere hides the same -cid-.
Think 'sequel' and 'sequence': what FOLLOWS. Seguimi! = Follow me!
Just like 'indicate'. Mi indica la strada? = Can you show me the way?
Can you show me the way?
Think 'discuss' (it can also mean a heated argument).
Think 'fumes'. Signs say VIETATO FUMARE = No smoking.
Think 'veto': to forbid. VIETATO = forbidden, on every Italian sign.
Pre (before) + notare (note down): you NOTE your name BEFORE you arrive. Ho prenotato = I booked.
Sounds like 'a fit': you rent a flat that's a good FIT. AFFITTASI = For rent.
Portare (to carry) + via (away). Da portare via = to go / takeaway.
Picture a stick figure: 'I' with an 'O' head = IO, that's ME.
Like old English 'thou'. Use it with friends and kids.
LOUIS: picture a man called Louis. Lui = HE.
Sounds like 'lay': SHE wears a Hawaiian lei. With a capital, Lei = polite 'you'.
Sounds like 'noise': WE make a lot of noise together.
Sounds like 'voice': you all, raise your VOICES!
Sounds like 'Laura': THEY all know Laura. Il loro = their.
Just one letter. With a vowel after it, it can become 'ed': ed io.
Sounds like 'or' without the r. Caffè o tè? = Coffee or tea?
Sounds like 'Ma!': 'Ma, but I want it!'
Ch = K in Italian. Che bello! = How lovely!
Like 'non-' in 'nonstop' and 'nonsense'. Always goes before the verb.
Sounds like 'see': 'See? YES!' Keep the accent: sì = yes, si = oneself.
Same as English. No, grazie = No, thanks.
Sounds like 'ankle': my ankle hurts TOO. Anch'io! = Me too!
Looks like English 'come' but means HOW. Come stai? = How are you?
Latin quando = when. Quando arrivi? = When do you get here?
Looks like the bird 'dove', but means WHERE. Picture asking: where is the dove?
Per (for) + che (what) = for what? Answers 'why' and 'because'.
Sounds like 'say': SAY IF you want to come.
Sounds like 'pew': in church, MORE and more people fill the PEWs. Di più = more.
Think 'minus' and 'menu' (MEN-OO). Più o meno = more or less.
'Poco a poco' = little by little. Music also uses 'poco' for 'a little'.
'Tutti frutti' = all the fruits. Tutto bene? = All good?
Sounds like 'Nyet, NOTHING!' Non è niente = It's nothing.
Sounds like 'only': not only one, but EVERY one. Ogni giorno = every day.
Think 'alternative' and 'alter ego': the OTHER one.
Sounds like 'stressed': the SAME stress every day. È lo stesso = It's all the same.
Sounds like 'question': THIS question right here.
Sounds like 'cello': THAT cello over there.
Starts like 'me' and 'my'. Il mio libro = my book.
Tu (you) + o: tuo = your. È tuo? = Is it yours?
Matches the THING owned, not the owner: la sua macchina = his OR her car.
'Cosa Nostra' = OUR thing. La nostra casa = our house.
Voi (you all) + -stro, like nostro. Il vostro amico = your friend.
Like 'de' in names: Leonardo da Vinci, Marco DI Rossi. Il libro di Marco = Marco's book.
Used for going to cities and home: a Roma, a casa.
Leonardo DA Vinci = Leonardo FROM Vinci. Da Marco = at Marco's place.
Same as English. Used with countries: in Italia.
Think 'con' as in 'chili con carne' (with meat). Caffè con latte.
Sounds like 'sue': SUE stands ON the table. Sul tavolo = on the table.
The book is on the table.
Like 'per' in 'per person' and 'per cent'. Per te = for you.
Like 'trans-': across, between. Tra un'ora = in an hour.
Sounds like 'sotto voce' (said quietly, below the voice). Under the bed.
The cat is under the bed.
'Soprano' = the HIGHEST voice, above the others.
Think 'dentist': he looks INSIDE your mouth. Vieni dentro! = Come inside!
